deductions_checked: Integral imbalance correction: epsilon=k/h<=1 makes the fractional cut-feasible flow compatible with original capacity1. Place divergence supplies at v_in and give the internal split edge v_in->v_out capacity ceil(kn/h). Its flow equals total outgoing original flow, at most epsilon(n-1). Integer flow gives outdegree<=M and indegree<=M+k. Bound each cut by the smaller-side outgoing or complementary incoming budget.

Balanced edge split: transferring a correcting arc subset from blue to red cancels both opposite divergence vectors. Red expansion cannot decrease; blue loses at most M+k per smaller-side vertex. At n<=D^1.02,h>=cD^.90, k=O(D^.51 sqrt(log D)), M=O(D^.63 sqrt(log D)), so both retain expansion at the same exponent.

Sampling exponent .77: witness-family concentration in source proof does not depend on tau; h²/n>=c²D^.78 dominates O(D^.12 log²D) counting cost. The approximation needs tau log(n)/h=o(1), giving D^(-.13)log D; the final perturbation needs tau n log(n)/h²=o(1), giving D^(-.01)log D. Both hold uniformly.

For the sampled directed graph, outgoing plus incoming cut sizes dominate the merged underlying undirected cut; their difference is the divergence sum. Pointwise imbalance k bounds its absolute value by k times the smaller side. Thus each direction has expansion at least (D^.77-k)/2. Correction inside the induced graph removes O(D^.76 sqrt(log D)) degrees and leaves a balanced expanding reservoir and balanced global complement.
